evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Add the definitions the finance mart doesn't have yet (ARR, renewal rate, churn, CAC), versioned in dbt and documented in Unity Catalog, with the tests that make each one defensible
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Rigour — defensibility, tests, reconciliation, automated checks and lineage recur throughout; the one speed reference ('a week of modeling work is now an afternoon') is about AI leverage, not shipping pressure.
evidence.domain_risk: you'll own the metrics, reporting and reconciliation our financial decisions rest on ... feeding the CFO's forecast and board reporting
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: High — the outputs feed CFO forecasting, board reporting and ledger reconciliation, so errors land directly in financial reporting.
evidence.data_team_maturity: Our dbt project is live on Databricks with a star-schema finance mart in production and documented in Unity Catalog.
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: Mid — a production dbt/Databricks platform, semantic layer and internal AI agent already exist, but it is explicitly 'a small team supporting four brands' rather than a specialised org.
evidence.jd_authorship: Move the recurring finance pack into marimo, retire the Tableau views behind it, and turn a monthly hand-build into something that runs on a schedule.
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: hiring_manager — every bullet names the specific artefact, tool and current state (marimo, Unity Catalog, star-schema finance mart), so the actual work is unmistakable.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: Subscription metrics you've built and defended to a finance stakeholder: ARR/MRR, renewal, churn, LTV/CAC, or cohort revenue.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: Finance — the audience is Finance, Accounting and the CFO, with board reporting and reconciliation to the ledger as the primary outputs.
evidence.autonomy_level: What's missing is the layer on top, and that layer is yours.
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: Strategic — the candidate owns the metric layer end to end, defines the governed definitions, and decides what escalates upstream.
evidence.ai_role: We also run an internal AI agent that answers business questions in Slack off the semantic layer, so every metric you define and test becomes a question Finance can ask directly rather than queue.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: ai_enabler — the candidate's modelled metrics are what the internal AI agent answers from, and they are also expected to work daily with Claude Code and agent SDKs; the tie-breaker resolves to enabler.
evidence.testing_framing: Route discrepancies upstream with the evidence attached and turn each one into a test. You build the checks and escalate.
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Responsibility — the candidate builds the automated checks and converts each reconciliation break into a test they own.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: unwilling to let a number you can't explain go out the door ... A spreadsheet nobody can reproduce reads to you as a liability.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: High — the role is framed around producing 'numbers the business can defend' and catching discrepancies before close, with financial and board exposure as the stake.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: You won't start from scratch. Our dbt project is live on Databricks with a star-schema finance mart in production ... What's missing is the layer on top, and that layer is yours.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: Mixed — a new governed metric and forecasting layer is built greenfield on top of an already-productionised platform, while Tableau views are retired and a manual monthly pack is migrated.
evidence.loss_aversion: 'Reconcile transactions across the app stores, payment processors, subscription systems and the ledger, with automated checks that alert rather than surface at close' — the fear is a discrepancy reaching the financial close undetected.
